'''Premiere - Cloud City (Modified)''' is a retro constructed format: the [[Premiere - Cloud City]] card pool with a ban list, used each year since 2024 for Event 2 of the [[Retro League]]. The league's announcement says it "transports you back to 1997", to the last era of cards from ''A New Hope'' and ''The Empire Strikes Back'' only and before starting interrupts, but with a series of cards banned, mostly from [[Dagobah]], that lead to a negative player experience.<ref name="pc-gemp" /><ref name="t85238" />

* '''Type:''' constructed
* '''Defined by:''' Players Committee [[Retro League]] (2024)
* '''Card pool:''' Premiere through Cloud City, with a ban list
* '''In use:''' 2024 &ndash;
* '''Also called:''' P-Cloud City (modified), Premiere to Cloud City (modified), PCCM<ref name="t85238" /><ref name="t86593" />
* '''[[GEMP]]:''' ''Premiere - Cloud City (Modified)'' (<code>premiere_cc_m</code>) on both the Players Committee GEMP and play.swccg.com

== Card pool ==
Its card pool is the same as [[Premiere - Cloud City]], Decipher set ids 1&ndash;5 and premium ids 101&ndash;105, with a ban list.<ref name="pc-gemp" /> The GEMP format definition sets no deck size, so GEMP uses its default of 60 cards.<ref name="gemp" /><ref name="lib" />

=== Ban list ===
GEMP bans these cards:<ref name="pc-gemp" /><ref name="cardjson" />
* Light Side: ''Never Tell Me The Odds'', ''Asteroid Sanctuary'', ''Anger, Fear, Aggression'', ''Clouds''
* Dark Side: ''3,720 To 1'', ''A Dangerous Time'', ''Defensive Fire'', ''Clouds'', ''Scanning Crew''
The 2024 Retro League used the first seven.<ref name="t84002" /> ''Clouds'' (Dark) and ''Scanning Crew'' were added for 2025,<ref name="t85234" /><ref name="t85238" /> and the list was unchanged in 2026.<ref name="t86593" />

== History ==
The format joined the Retro League in 2024 as Event 2.<ref name="t84002" /> It has been used for:
* [[2024 Retro League Event 2]], 24 March &ndash; 8 May 2024, won by [[Paul Todd Feldman]].<ref name="t83974" />
* [[2025 Retro League Event 2]], 16 March &ndash; 27 April 2025, won by [[Paul Todd Feldman]].<ref name="t85238" />
* [[2026 Retro League Event 2]], 29 March &ndash; 10 May 2026, won by [[Joe Horbey]].<ref name="t86593" /><ref name="email20260518" />
For 2025, Retro League player [[Andy Talaga]] wrote a metagame guide to the format, attached to the event thread.<ref name="t85238" />
